notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1; all parts are in the catalogue.

Circuit: each FSR runs from the 5V rail to an analog node (A0 / A1) with a 10K resistor from that node to the GND rail (voltage divider). The pushbutton joins 5V to pin 2, and a 10K pull-down resistor on the pin 2 side goes to GND.

Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue scheme (top half bank 't' rows a-e, bottom half bank 'b' rows f-j), so the row letters differ from the letters printed on the image. Only the column-bank strip matters electrically. Rail hole numbers are approximate positions read from the image.
Rails: tp/tn are the top + and - rails, bp/bn the bottom + and - rails. Wires 8 and 9 link the top and bottom rails on the right.

Pushbutton legs straddle the centre gap in columns 5 and 7. Side 1 (1.l/1.r) is column 5, linked top to bottom, and side 2 (2.l/2.r) is column 7. Pressing joins column 5 (5V) to column 7 (pin 2 plus pull-down).
FSR pin 1 is taken as the leg going to the + rail (red leg in the image) and pin 2 as the leg going to the sense column. The FSR is symmetric so this choice does not matter.
Wire ends are given port 'a' for the Arduino or rail end and 'b' for the breadboard hole end, as an arbitrary choice.
